The cornemuse du Centre is the bagpipe of the central French regions of Bourbonnais, Berry, Nivernais and Morvan, and belongs to the bagpipe family. The chanter carries a double reed of cane or plastic; two wooden drone pipes can be tuned by sliding and stand one and two octaves below the keynote, using single reeds. Playing is largely chromatic, and modern instruments can sound every semitone, but usually not in equal temperament, to suit the drones; because the drones are fixed, the keys commonly used are mostly the tonic or the dominant. The treble model mostly uses semi-closed fingering, and chanters of twenty inches and more mostly use open fingering; notable players include Eric Montbel, Jean Blanchard, Robert Amyott and Julien Barbances.
演奏時以風袋供氣，吹管裝雙簧片，兩支低音管裝單簧片。高音吹管多用半閉指法，下手指: The bag supplies the air, the chanter carries a double reed and the two drone pipes carry single reeds. The treble chanter mostly uses semi-closed fingering, the lower hand covering the holes in step with the upper; chanters of 20 inches and more mostly use open fingering. A beginner should first settle the key, since the drones cannot change key and playing is usually confined to the tonic or the dominant; modern instruments can play semitones, but not in equal temperament, and must be matched to the drones.
